author: owner
title: Owner: no model context; string targets with a closed role set
body:
Journal #7: the formalizer input is the user message only (no shortlist, identifiers, knowledge or clock). Targets are quoted strings: a relation phrase plus roles from the closed set subject, object, recipient, location, source, destination, instrument, time, topic. The host links strings to the lexicon.

Now the non-negotiable "Model boundary" section of AGENTS.md, guarded by `tests/model-input-boundary.test.mjs`, `tests/no-context-lint.test.mjs` and the corpus-audit check `vocabulary.model_target_id_token`.

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

author: owner
title: Owner: no model-level refusal
body:
Journal #9: the model never refuses; every message is formalized. What the reasoner can conclude is decided by the host, not by the model.

Relevant later: prompted Haiku without thinking answered 176 real wild-suite queries with `unclear kind no_request`, i.e. it judged answerability, which this rule forbids (see baselines).

author: review-agent
title: No-context sweep: 435 findings; the training projection still sent CONTEXT
body:
Journal #15 and `eval/reports/current/no-context-sweep.md`. A read-only sweep for everything that still gave the small model context found **435 findings**: model input 48, model output 118, training data 98, data QA 135, host 7, docs 29.

- `server/llm.mjs` `barePrompt` defaulted to the sop-agent-3 profile, producing CONTEXT + MESSAGE for any caller that omitted it.
- The training projection (`tools/research/prepare-experiment.mjs`) built prompts from `context_assertions` + question with the row's `context`.
- 122,441 derived prompt rows started with CONTEXT, including all 121,166 rows of `datasets/research-train-v1`, the trainer's input; 14,225 carried background knowledge.
- No corpus had a single string-target (sop-agent-4) row.

Later status (header of the report, same day): most findings were in corpora and builders deleted with the DS022 regeneration; permanent guards G1–G4 now exist.

Seeded on 2026-09-29 from the journal and reports; the timestamp is that of the source event.

body:
Journal #65: DS021 section "Input languages and English canonical output", English relation/value/time/reading rules, cross-lingual anchoring, ambiguity tolerance via `sop_targets_accepted`; wire help pages, wiki, training page and `server/prompts/formalizer.txt` give English targets for Romanian examples. **Open at the time:** the `server/agent.mjs` stated-anchoring guard still rejected translated common-noun values. The Haiku validity review later found one case where this guard voided a faithful 57-statement program ("ședința cu părinții" → "the meeting with parents").

author: Fable review
title: What the English-target rule costs a 135M–270M model on Romanian
body:
From the Fable data-improvement plan §1.5 and questions.md D1:

- Relation phrases whose content words occur in the message: English train 91.5%, Romanian train **4.7%**, wild Romanian 8.7%. For Romanian the model must translate, not copy.
- The whole RO→EN relation "dictionary" in training is **104** construction pairs.
- Romanian OOD tolerant execution: SmolLM2-135M 8.4% and Gemma 3 270M 13.1% overall (English 54.0% and 40.5%); on the held-out-domain axis SmolLM2 4.6%, Gemma 3.6%, prompted Haiku 38.5%.
- 64.5% of real (wild) Romanian messages have no diacritics, against 12.8% in training; SmolLM2 spends 2.59 tokens per Romanian word against 1.61 for English.

The plan proposes an A/B experiment (E3) between a large RO→EN dictionary in the data and Romanian lemma targets linked by the host (owner decision D1, open).

author: translate-eval-agent
title: Translation changes the names the targets keep as written
body: Targets keep proper names and titles exactly as written in the message (e.g. "Grădina Botanică din Timișoara"). Any whole-message translator breaks that: name fidelity of the translation was 0.30 (Gemma 270M-it base), 0.55 (SmolLM2-360M base), 0.68 (Opus-MT roa-en); Opus-MT strips diacritics (Galați -> Galatii, Bogdan-Ionuț -> Bogdan-Ionut) and rewrites code-switched English (leases -> reads). Yet Opus-MT fixes exactly the content-word failure (lavandă -> lavender, ardei -> peppers). This supports D1: the model keeps the message's strings, the host translates only normalized content words, never names, quotes or English spans.

author: model-language-agent
title: Owner: content words in either language; the host dictionary makes it fine either way
body:
Owner (refinement of D1, 2026-09-29): "we don't mind if it doesn't translate, we don't mind if it does; build synonym and translation dictionaries so that we can verify quickly and it's fine either way".

What this means in the system:
- Training targets keep ONE convention: content words in the message's language, normalized (relation lemmas such as "lucra la", common nouns in the nominative such as "sala de sport"); Romanian stays Romanian, a mixed message keeps each word in its own language, proper names stay as written, keywords are English (DS021 "Input languages and content words", DS022 item 3).
- The host and the evaluation are language-agnostic: `sop/dictionary.mjs` maps Romanian lemmas and inflected forms, English phrases and their synonyms to the same entry ("lucra la", "work at", "be employed by", "fi angajat la" → works_at). Linking retries a string that does not link with the dictionary's translations and synonyms in tiers; the host lexicon decides; an unknown Romanian word is reported `untranslated`, never guessed.
- The dictionary is systematic and reviewable: `config/dictionary/manual.tsv` (reviewed hand entries), `generator.tsv` (every RO/EN surface of the generator's predicates), `wiktionary.tsv` (filtered English Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 4.0, DS014); `tools/dictionary.mjs propose|review|approve` adds a synonym found by evaluation; the compiled lookup maps are cached under state/cache/dictionary/ keyed by the sources' SHA-256.
- Evaluation keeps the strict score (no dictionary) and adds the tolerant one (dictionary and synonyms) for execution equivalence, canonical match and the wild accepted match (DS016).

author: model-language-agent
title: Honest partial formalization: the unparsed wire and symbolic repair
body:
Owner idea (2026-09-29): small models give up or invent; instead they should formalize what they understood and put what they did not understand in special wires that symbolic heuristics repair. Measured on wild: fine-tuned models give up on only 2-9% of content rows, but corrupt about 15% of names and invent about 8% of values, so the goal is honest partial formalization.
- New model wire `unparsed`: `span` (verbatim part of the message, anchored by the agent guard, unparsed_span_not_in_message), optional `near $id` and `hint` (subject, object, time, location, value, relation, reference, other; exported UNPARSED_HINTS). Several are allowed; unclear gibberish/no_request stay for whole messages. The role the span would fill holds a placeholder ?variable, also in stated/assumed, paired by near + hint (an unpaired placeholder is rejected, proposition_not_ground).
- Host repair before linking (`sop/repair.mjs`): dates/times, numbers/money/units, conversation references from caller-owned context (only with exactly one candidate), proper names, the dictionary. Resolved spans fill their slot (packet `repairs`); each unresolved span becomes one targeted question (`unresolved_spans`), only the wires that need it are held back, and the rest of the message is answered.
- Evaluation: honesty_ratio = marked / (marked + invented), invented_value_rate, and understood F1 (wire F1 excluding gold wires whose value lies in a predicted unparsed span) (DS016).
